turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt900_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (O, Sb, Co, Si, Sn, Ca, Ni, Ti, Pb, Se, Ge, Cu, Zr, Te, S, Zn,
    Fe, Yb, Mn, Sr, Nb, Bi, Cd, Hf, In) and `target` (the measured zT
    (thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K).
  - b3_te_zt900_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 900 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the training data

**Which chemistries dominate the high-zT tail (train zT > 1.2)?**

| family | representative training rows | zT |
|---|---|---|
| Pb–Te (+S / +Se / +Sr) | Pb .494/Te .346/S .148 → 2.21; Pb .32/Te .61/Se .05 → 2.26; Pb .476/Te .495/Sr .019 → 2.03; Pb .494/Te .46/S .04 → 1.28 | **1.3–2.3** |
| Pb–Se (near 1:1) | Pb .48/Se .50 → 1.40; Pb .475/Se .50 → 1.24; Pb .479/Se .504/Sb .017 → 1.62 | **1.2–1.6** |
| Cu₂Se (Cu/Se ≈ 2) | 1.17, 1.45, 1.74 (one outlier 0.40) | **~1.2 avg, up to 1.7** |
| Sn–Ni–Zr–Hf half-Heusler | 1.21, 1.32, 1.35 (many ~0.9–1.0) | ~1.0 |
| Pb–S, Sn–Te, Sb–Fe–Nb–Ti, Sb–Yb–Mn | 0.7–1.14 | ≤1.1 |

Everything oxide-based (O-containing perovskites, ZnO, Ca/Mn oxides, Co-oxides) sits below ~0.35, and Si/Ge/Fe silicides ≤0.9. So the pool should be screened for **Pb-chalcogenides, Cu₂Se, and Sn/PbTe alloys**.

**Pool screening**

- **c052** = Pb .493 / Te .394 / S .099 → sits exactly between the two best PbTe–PbS training points (S = 0.04 → 1.28; S = 0.148 → 2.21). Predicted **≈1.8–1.9**, clearly the best.
- **c012** = Pb .500 / Se .498 → at the top of the PbSe Pb-rich trend (1.19 → 1.24 → 1.40 as Pb rises). Predicted **≈1.4–1.5**.
- **c054** (Cu .651/Se .326) and **c063** (Cu .664/Se .336) → Cu₂Se stoichiometry, training mean ≈1.2 with upside to 1.7.
- **c097** (Sn .485/Te .50/Mn .015) and **c025** (Sn .485/Te .50/In .015) → SnTe alloys, training analogue (Sn/Te/Mn) = 1.05.
- Rejected: PbTe + Bi (c001, c006, c041) — the only Bi-doped PbTe in training gives just 0.68; PbS + In (c008, c021) ≈0.8–1.0; half-Heuslers c035/c078/c093 ≈0.95–1.0; Sb–Fe–Nb–Ti (c002, c009, c023, c034, c095) ≈0.9–1.05 (high Nb hurts); Yb–Sb–Mn (c044, c060, c070) ≈0.7–0.8; all oxide/silicide entries ≪1.

Final: c052, c012, c054, c063, c097
